- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 30d forecast), especially when sentiment is neutral or rising — apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from peak forecast days.
- Forecast mean reverts to 10–15% of 30d history average within 5–7 days after spike — adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average if sentiment is weak.
- If 30d forecast is >10% above 30d history mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.85).
- If 30d forecast is <10% below 30d history mean, increase by 5–10% if sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) to avoid underestimation bias.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment drops sharply within 3–5 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 5 days.
